summary: Privacy-focused Tauri browser shell with passing TypeScript, policy, Rust, production build, session isolation, permission, download, audit, WebView contract, and live WebView binding validation. Recent work fixed silent-failure bugs, an isolation-scope cleanup leak, a disconnected vault bookmark count, corrected UI/audit claims that overstated session isolation as real storage separation (it is currently bookkeeping-only), replaced the encrypted-export key derivation with Argon2id, and moved the permission/download decision registries from in-memory-only to SQLite persistence.
current_objective: Validate the live WebView privacy boundary through bounded manual use without expanding architecture; keep claims honest as gaps are found.
next_action: No specific outstanding action. Permission/download registries now persist and were verified against a real packaged-app quit/relaunch cycle. Remaining v1.1_PLAN.md scope (SQLCipher, OS keychain, WebView permission/download callback integration) not started; the last item is blocked on the same gap as session-storage isolation (see docs/recommendations/SESSION_STORAGE_ISOLATION_SCOPE.md).
known_gaps: Session isolation is TypeScript-layer bookkeeping only; there is one shared WebView, so cookies/storage are not actually partitioned per profile.
SQLCipher at-rest encryption and OS keychain integration remain planned.
constraints: Do not add a new browser subsystem during validation.
Do not weaken download blocking or permission prompting.
Do not treat smoke tests as proof of packaged desktop behavior.
Manual validation must use bounded, non-sensitive test URLs and content.
Do not let UI copy, audit events, or the threat model claim privacy guarantees that aren't actually implemented.
